sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicant submits that although allegation of rape has been alleged against the applicant on which basis cognizance has been taken and summons have been issued but the aspect that the applicant is husband of the informant has been totally lost sight of.

It is submitted that even in the statement given to the police which is a part of case diary, the informant has admitted that she was married to applicant and therefore there was no occasion for summons having been issued under Section 376 IPC.
5.

Learned Additional Government Advocate has opposed the application with the submission that the statement of informant recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. clearly corroborate allegations levelled in the first information report.

He has also drawn attention to the aforesaid statements to submit that the marriage between the two as alleged has been indicated having been performed by using force upon informant while she was already married to another person.

6. Upon consideration of submissions advanced by learned counsel for parties and perusal of material on record, it appears that allegations of rape have been alleged against applicant by the informant.

The said allegations have thereafter been corroborated by the informant in her statements recorded under Sections 161 & 164 Cr.P.C. in which although she admits a Nikahnama and a notary affidavit being executed between the applicant and the informant pertaining to marriage but states that the said documents were prepared under coercion and force exerted by the applicant.

The aspect of whether the informant and the applicant are married or not as on the date of occurrence of incident is the subject matter of evidence and will be required to be adjudicated upon by trial court at the appropriate stage.
7.
The summoning order has clearly been issued on the basis of contents of first information report and statements of informant without adverting to any extraneous material.
8. In view of aforesaid, this Court does not find any occasion to interfere with the order impugned.
9. The application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. being devoid of merits is dismissed.
